why_this_file_exists: MATCHING-GOLDEN-2026-09-02.json is a DATED ARTIFACT and is never rewritten. But an adjudication can be wrong, and the commonest way for it to be wrong is that it recorded the world as it was on the day of capture rather than the answer that was always true: a market with no correct event, versus a market whose correct event our own bug hid from us. Correcting that by hand-editing tests/fixtures/matching_golden_inputs.json would work exactly once — capture_matching_golden_fixture.py re-derives correct_event_id straight from the artifact, so the next re-capture would silently revert it and the ratchet would cry regression all over again with nobody able to see why. So corrections live HERE, as data, with their evidence, and the capture script applies them. Every amendment is a claim about truth that a reader can check.
rules: An amendment names the market, what the artifact said, what it should say, and WHY — with evidence that can be re-run, not an assertion.

It is applied BEFORE the pair is built, so search_surfaced_the_answer and the adjudicated-event-must-be-present guarantee are both recomputed against the corrected answer rather than patched afterwards.

`was` is asserted against the artifact. If the artifact does not say what the amendment claims it says, the capture FAILS rather than applying a correction to a pair that has already moved underneath it.

An amendment never turns a FAILING pair green by itself. It changes the adjudicated answer; the baseline is then re-recorded and the ratchet reports the movement in whichever direction it really went.
Amendments are append-only. Superseding one means adding another that names it.

amendments.why: The artifact recorded `correct_event_id: null` for a `d-mislabel` pair, and for that class null never meant 'this market belongs on no event' — all 200 d-mislabel pairs carry null. It meant the market was mislabelled and the target was left unresolved. Here the target exists and is unambiguous: the Kalshi ticker KXKNVBCUPGAME-26SEP02GSVROO names the KNVB cup tie of 2026-09-02, and event 15297322 is 'Gsv 28' vs 'Roosendaal' on 2026-09-02. The reason the matcher could not reach it on the day of capture was that `kxknvbcupgame` was unmapped, so the market's LLM category ('legal') decided its sport. That is our bug, not the market's truth.
evidence: Production census 2026-09-06 00:00Z over every event whose team names match %Roosendaal% or %Gsv%: event 15297322 (Gsv 28 vs Roosendaal, soccer_other, 2026-09-02, scheduled) is the ONLY row for that tie. There is no rival to prefer, so `null` cannot have meant 'it belongs on a different event'.

The whole soccer_other Slovak/Dutch cup population has external_id NULL — the Odds API does not cover these cups — so 'it was auto-created' cannot be the disqualifier either, or the class has no correct answer at all.
Replayed with the four cup keys added to KALSHI_TICKER_TO_SPORT_KEY: `replay()` returns (15297322, 'matched'). Without them it returns (None, 'no_match'). The ticker mapping is the whole difference.

amendments.why: Same class and same cause as 59700960. KXSVKCUPGAME-26SEP02PUCTRN names the Slovak cup tie of 2026-09-02; event 15297301 is 'Puchov' vs 'Trnava' on 2026-09-02.
evidence: Production census 2026-09-06 00:00Z over %Trnava% / %Puchov%: 33 events match, and exactly one is the Puchov-Trnava tie — 15297301. The other 32 are Spartak Trnava league fixtures against other opponents.

This pair is the harder of the two and it is the reason to be confident rather than the reason to hesitate: six candidates are on offer and five of them are decoy `FC Spartak Trnava vs FC Košice - <prop>` rows. The matcher picks 15297301, which is the restraint the fixture exists to test.
Replayed with the four cup keys added: (15297301, 'matched'). Without them: (None, 'no_match').

amendments.why: Third of the class, same cause as 59700960 and 59701032: a `d-mislabel` pair whose `null` meant 'target left unresolved', not 'this market belongs on no event'. lane1/145 held it back because, unlike the first two, the ticker date and the chosen event's date DISAGREE by two days — KXLEAGUESCUPSPREAD-26SEP02TOLLEO says 26SEP02, event 15293431 says 2026-08-31 23:00Z — and that is exactly the discrepancy that separates an amendment from a mis-link. Read at the venue, the disagreement resolves the other way round from the way it was feared: THE TICKER DATE IS RIGHT AND OUR EVENT'S STORED DATE IS WRONG. Kalshi lists exactly one Toluca-Leon tie in Leagues Cup, on Sep 2; event 15293431 is a soccer_concacaf_leagues_cup Toluca vs Leon; so it is the same tie and the attachment is correct. The two-day gap is a date defect on OUR event row, not evidence that the prop is pointing at a different match. Amended.
evidence: Venue-side read of Kalshi's own API 2026-09-06 10:45Z, by series discovery rather than a guessed ticker (standing notice 26): GET /trade-api/v2/events/KXLEAGUESCUPSPREAD-26SEP02TOLLEO returns series_ticker KXLEAGUESCUPSPREAD, product_metadata.competition 'Leagues Cup', title 'Toluca vs Leon: Regulation Time Spread' and sub_title 'TOL vs LEO (Sep 2)'. The market is unambiguously about the LEAGUES CUP tie, and Kalshi itself dates that tie Sep 2.

Scanned all three Leagues Cup prop series at the venue (KXLEAGUESCUPSPREAD / KXLEAGUESCUPTOTAL / KXLEAGUESCUPBTTS, 60 settled events each): EXACTLY ONE Toluca-Leon event in each, all *-26SEP02TOLLEO, all sub_title 'TOL vs LEO (Sep 2)'. There is no Aug 31 Toluca-Leon at the venue, so `null` cannot have meant 'it belongs on a rival tie' and the candidate is unambiguous.

Production 2026-09-06 10:44Z, every %Toluca% event between 2026-08-25 and 2026-09-10: event 15293431 is (Toluca, Leon, 2026-08-31 23:00Z, closed, soccer_concacaf_leagues_cup / 'Leagues Cup'). SAME COMPETITION as the market. The Liga MX reading that would have made this a genuine mis-link — both clubs are Liga MX, so an Aug 31 league fixture two days before a Sep 2 cup tie is entirely plausible — is refuted by the sport key: 15293431 is keyed to Leagues Cup, and Toluca's Liga MX rows in the same window are against Juarez, not Leon.

What fixes the true match time, and therefore which side of the two-day gap is wrong: the market's own early-close contract is 'This market will close and expire after a winner is declared', its status is `finalized`, and its close_time is 2026-09-03T03:36:31Z — late on Sep 2 in Mexico. A market that settles on winner-declaration cannot close on Sep 3 for a match played Aug 31. occurrence_datetime is 2026-09-03T05:00:00Z.

And the fixture's own market commence_time of 2026-09-05 07:00Z, which looks like a third date, is not one: it is EXACTLY the market's latest_expiration_time (2026-09-05T07:00:00Z) read off the venue. We stored Kalshi's settlement backstop where a start time belongs — the #3438 class — so that value is evidence about our ingest, not about the tie.

FOLLOW-ON, filed not fixed under D35 and belonging to lane1 under D39, NOT a condition of this amendment: (a) event 15293431's commence_time is wrong by ~2 days against the venue; (b) event 15294151 'Deportivo Toluca FC vs Club Leon FC' (soccer_other, 2026-08-28 16:15:23Z, closed) looks like a second row for this same tie — two rows for one game, the #2693 bar.

amendments.why: Fourth of the class, same cause as 59700960, 59701032 and 59700871: a `d-mislabel` pair whose `null` meant 'target left unresolved', not 'this market belongs on no event'. This is the EASIEST of the four and it is worth saying why, because the previous one was the hardest. 59700871 had to survive a genuine two-day disagreement between the ticker date and the event date. This pair has no such gap to explain away: ticker `26AUG26` and event `2026-08-27 00:30Z` are the same evening either side of the UTC midnight line (Aug 26, 19:30 CDT in Toluca), and the venue's own close_time for the contract is 2026-08-27T03:03:57Z -- about 2.5h after that kickoff, which is what a 90-minute match settles like. The competition is not inferred from the ticker letters: Kalshi's own product_metadata names it. Amended.
evidence: Venue-side read of Kalshi's own API 2026-09-06 ~18:30Z, browser UA (standing notice 26): GET /trade-api/v2/events/KXLEAGUESCUPGAME-26AUG26TOLATX?with_nested_markets=true returns series_ticker KXLEAGUESCUPGAME, product_metadata.competition 'Leagues Cup', competition_scope 'Regulation Time Moneyline', title 'Toluca vs Austin: Regulation Time Moneyline' and sub_title 'TOL vs ATX (Aug 26)'. All three legs (-TOL/-ATX/-TIE) carry rules_primary '... the Toluca vs Austin professional Leagues Cup soccer game originally scheduled for Aug 26, 2026 ...'. The venue NAMES the competition; it is not read off the ticker letters.

Venue-side uniqueness by SERIES DISCOVERY, not a guessed ticker (notice 26): scanned all 60 settled events of series KXLEAGUESCUPGAME. EXACTLY ONE is a Toluca-Austin tie -- KXLEAGUESCUPGAME-26AUG26TOLATX, sub_title 'TOL vs ATX (Aug 26)'. There is no rival tie at the venue, so `null` cannot have meant 'it belongs on a different Toluca-Austin match'.

Production 2026-09-06 ~18:35Z, every %Toluca% or %Austin FC% event between 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-30: FOUR rows, and exactly one pairs the two clubs -- event 15291291 (Toluca, Austin FC, 2026-08-27 00:30:00Z, completed, soccer_concacaf_leagues_cup, external_id a757053929c339a085eea0fc463f85ce). SAME COMPETITION as the market. The other three are different fixtures entirely (Austin FC v Colorado Rapids, Deportivo Toluca v Club Leon, Toluca v Juarez). The candidate is unambiguous on our side as well as the venue's.

The adjudicated candidate is PRESENT in the pair's own captured candidate set (event 15291291 is one of its 10 events), so the pair is winnable rather than being amended to an answer the replay could never reach -- the guarantee the capture script would otherwise recompute.

The `null` was recorded under the exact condition this change removes: the pair's note is `non-sport-category;cup-ticker` and the market's stored llm_sport_category at capture was `legal`. With `kxleaguescupgame` unmapped, an LLM category of 'legal' decided the market's sport, so the matcher could not reach a soccer event at all. That is our bug, not the market's truth -- the same sentence as the three amendments above.

Replayed on the real harness with the prefix mapped: `replay()` returns (15291291, 'matched'). Without the mapping it returns (None, 'no_match'). The ticker mapping is the whole difference, and the golden suite is green on the combined tree with the baseline UNMOVED at 652 -- the pair passed before as a correct `None` and passes after as a correct 15291291.

NOT a condition of this amendment, filed under D35 and belonging to lane1 under D39: our stored market commence_time for 59173468 is 2026-08-27 03:03:57Z, which is EXACTLY the venue's close_time for all three legs -- we again stored a Kalshi settlement stamp where a start time belongs (the #3438 / #3532 class).
